column1: # What a hoisted-sail heading key and the synthesized repeats print.
# `commands.md §5.2`: "Outdoor movement prints its compass word followed by a
# newline." Under hoisted sail that is narrowed by u5-spec#297: the
# turn-or-move test is against the ship's **facing**, not the cached sail
# direction (`weather.md §5`, `RETRACTIONS.md` R525). A key that changes the
# facing turns the ship in place and prints `Head <Dir>` (plus `Hull weak!`
# below hull 50) without moving; a key that keeps the facing prints nothing
# (`vehicles.md §6`) and attempts the step on that same command in any
# non-calm wind. The input helper then synthesizes repeated movement from the
# cached direction, and a wait pass prints nothing from the sailing logic.
# The overworld prompt pair (`text-output.md §10.2`, R526 amending R497): the
# flag is cleared only by a direction taken under hoisted sail, and a frigate
# facing change or an under-sail refusal sets it again in the same command.
# So `heading` - a course change - is followed by an ordinary pair: a blank
# row under `Hull weak!` and the end-cap row with the cursor, which stays put
# while the ship waits upwind. Each released step that keeps the facing
# suppresses exactly one following pair, so the synthesized repeats draw no
# new rows of their own; output a released step prints lands on the bare
# marker row its pair drew (`BREAKING UP!`, as `sail-calm` shows), except an
# encounter line, which starts the row below it.
# `sail-calm` (2026-10-16) caught the stock game, wind drifted to South,
# printing `>BREAKING UP!` straight under `>Yell HOIST!` - no `East` for a
# key that kept the facing or for the released step into the shoal. This
# scenario sails away from the coast instead, so the released steps are
# ordinary moves, and samples the window as they go.
# Encounter and wind dice from `sailing-more` on, measured 2026-10-16 over
# the four runs with this seed and these keys: by 8 s the stock side was hit
# by `* BOOM! *` and sunk (031944), attacked by SHARKS (204248) and by SEA
# HORSES (222947) - one run's stock capture never reached the game - and the
# engine's wind drifted to South on 222947 and ran it onto a shoal. Both
# stock attacks read `Hull weak!` / blank / the bare `>` row / `Attacked!`.
# Each wait pass is a consumed turn with its own encounter roll
# (`weather.md §5`), so only `hoisted`, `heading` and `sailing` are
# comparable, and `paired_compare.py` skips the later two beats by name - the
# deterministic three still report a difference as one.
# The `Head West` command is itself a consumed turn, so its own encounter
# roll can land before `heading`. rc2's sweep (`20261017-162039`) is that
# case: within 0.7 s the stock side printed `* BOOM! *` under `Hull weak!`
# and was `Ship sunk!` by `sailing`, while the engine drew nothing and printed
# exactly what rc1's run (`20261017-085852`) printed on both sides. Not an
# engine difference; a `heading`/`sailing` difference whose stock side shows
# an encounter line is that draw, and the run should simply be repeated. The
# two beats stay compared because they carry the prompt-row contract.

# requires-seed: profile `seed-drowning-collision` (frigate west of a coast)
